description: Glyph table of the Japanese ROM (Dark Law - Meaning of Death): which character each glyph key draws. Keys: one byte (single-byte page) or a prefix byte and an index (kanji pages). Built by reading the glyph sheets of tools/glyph_font.py and checking every kanji against its contexts in the text; see docs/re/glyph-table.md.

40.note: box with a diagonal; most uses are command arguments that the tokenizer reads as glyphs

B2.note: two ticks; follows ・ and page starts and precedes page breaks; may be a quotation mark or a decorative mark

BD.note: box with a diagonal; one use

FA 2A.note: blank glyph on a kanji page; used twice

FA 66.note: small red and white cross, used as punctuation after text (for example after 本当に)

FB 4C.note: context: この地の[ ]と闇を, [ ]が訪れた; shape not settled (災 is the best fit)

FB 69.note: read as 整; contexts: 整頓されて, 整然と

FB A2.note: context 堀当てま (probably a slip for 掘り当てました); the glyph is drawn with the earth radical
